name: network_interdiction_and_robust_placement
qualification: not_qualified: bounded deterministic reference with focused native kernel evidence; operator process tests require runtime build; no INT-FNX-001 or physical coverage qualification
tieBreak: maximum minimum action cost, then installation cost, cardinality and sensor tuple; loss ties by action count and typed identity tuple
complexityWitness: placement branches, action subsets, path searches and adjacency scans
outputSizeWitness: selected additions plus baseline and selected action sets, affected sensors and witness paths
objective: maximize the minimum total cost of individual sensor and shared failure actions opening an unobserved entry-to-target walk, subject to installation and addition-count ceilings
numericPolicy: separate named u64 installation and loss units; every individual and shared action cost is nonnegative and their total must fit u64; overlapping members are unioned and a selected shared action is charged once; installation feasibility uses checked subtraction
constraints: all existing placement preconditions and canonical semantics remain in force
every declared sensor retains one individual action at its declared disable cost
shared action IDs are unique within a separate typed namespace; a raw sensor/action label collision is legal
shared memberships are nonempty and name only declared baseline or candidate sensors
only installed members of a selected action are disabled; all declarations including inactive and unaffordable members bind the input digest
baseline and defended witness sensors are the union of active members, including explicitly declared zero-support sensors
no independence, failure probability, live health or effect authority is inferred
one work budget and cancellation source covers input admission, all placements and all action-set searches
no partial answer or heuristic fallback on refusal
a disconnected movement graph remains unreachable, never infinite robustness
compatibility: additive shared-failure API/report mode; original individual-loss placement and original interdiction input/output/decision/implementation identities and bytes remain unchanged
